changeSet.sql: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_uvl002_person_attribute_ai;
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_uvl002_person_attribute_au;
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_uvl002_person_attribute_ad;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_uvl002_person_attribute_ai AFTER INSERT ON person_attribute FOR EACH ROW UPDATE person p JOIN person_attribute_type pat ON pat.person_attribute_type_id = NEW.person_attribute_type_id SET p.date_changed = COALESCE(NEW.date_changed, NEW.date_created, NOW()), p.changed_by = COALESCE(NEW.changed_by, NEW.creator, p.changed_by) WHERE p.person_id = NEW.person_id AND pat.uuid = '9816ffad-781b-423f-a21d-1ab06afb4dcc';

CREATE TRIGGER trg_uvl002_person_attribute_au AFTER UPDATE ON person_attribute FOR EACH ROW UPDATE person p JOIN person_attribute_type pat ON pat.person_attribute_type_id IN (OLD.person_attribute_type_id, NEW.person_attribute_type_id) SET p.date_changed = COALESCE(NEW.date_changed, NOW()), p.changed_by = COALESCE(NEW.changed_by, NEW.creator, p.changed_by) WHERE p.person_id = NEW.person_id AND pat.uuid = '9816ffad-781b-423f-a21d-1ab06afb4dcc';

CREATE TRIGGER trg_uvl002_person_attribute_ad AFTER DELETE ON person_attribute FOR EACH ROW UPDATE person p JOIN person_attribute_type pat ON pat.person_attribute_type_id = OLD.person_attribute_type_id SET p.date_changed = COALESCE(OLD.date_changed, NOW()), p.changed_by = COALESCE(OLD.changed_by, OLD.creator, p.changed_by) WHERE p.person_id = OLD.person_id AND pat.uuid = '9816ffad-781b-423f-a21d-1ab06afb4dcc';

preConditions.sqlCheck: select count(*) from users where username = 'service-account-orthanc-service'

changeSet.comment:
OpenMRS user for the Keycloak service account the Orthanc EIP bridge presents.
oauth2login maps a token onto an OpenMRS user by preferred_username (openmrs.mapping.user.username), so a bearer token whose service account has no matching OpenMRS user is rejected exactly as basic auth is — 302 to /openmrs/oauth2login. That is why the bridge's POST /ws/rest/v1/obs never succeeded and no DICOM study ever became an attachment, while the equivalent call from the Odoo bridge did: service-account-eip already had a user here and service-account-orthanc-service did not.
Mirrors the roles service-account-eip holds. No usable password is set: the hash and salt are random, so the account can only ever authenticate by token.
Ids are resolved by subquery rather than hardcoded, unlike the older changesets above, so this cannot collide with rows added since. preConditions make it a no-op where the user already exists.
